subject: chemistry
title: Combined structure determination
key_idea: To deduce a structure, combine the evidence: elemental data for the empirical formula, M⁺ for the molecular formula, IR for the groups and NMR for the arrangement. Check the final structure against all of it.

sections.heading: What each type of data tells you

blocks.text: No single technique gives a full structure. This section covers what each piece of evidence adds.

rows: The empirical formula: the simplest ratio of atoms.
The relative molecular mass, so the molecular formula.
Pieces of the structure, from the masses lost or formed.
The bonds present, so the functional groups.
The number of carbon environments, and their types from δ.
The number of proton environments, how many protons in each, and their neighbours.

items: **Percentage composition**: divide each percentage by the element's relative atomic mass, then divide by the smallest answer to give the ratio.
**Combustion analysis**: burning a known mass of compound gives CO₂ and H₂O. The masses of these give the moles of carbon and hydrogen. Any mass missing is oxygen.
The **molecular formula** is a whole-number multiple of the empirical formula. The multiple is Mᵣ from the M⁺ peak ÷ the empirical formula mass.

blocks.label: Molecular formula
blocks.formula: multiple = Mᵣ of the compound ÷ empirical formula mass
where: Mᵣ: found from the molecular ion peak

items: Elemental data give the empirical formula; M⁺ then gives the molecular formula.
IR gives groups; NMR gives the arrangement.

sections.heading: A strategy for deducing a structure

blocks.text: Work through the data in a set order, and check the final structure against all of it.

diagram.alt: Put the steps for deducing a structure in order.
diagram.prompt: Put these steps in the order you would work
steps: Find the empirical formula from percentage composition or combustion data
Use the molecular ion peak to find the molecular formula
Use the IR spectrum to identify the functional groups
Use NMR to find how the atoms are arranged
Draw the structure and check it against every piece of data

items: Use the molecular formula to find the number of double bonds or rings. A saturated compound with no ring has 2n + 2 hydrogens for n carbons. Oxygen does not change this. Fewer hydrogens means a C=C, a C=O or a ring.
Each IR group you find must show up as the right peak or fragment in the other data.
If a structure does not fit one piece of data, it is wrong, even if it fits the others.
Take the data in order, from formula to groups to arrangement.
Check the answer against every piece of data.

blocks.text: A compound contains 48.6% carbon, 8.1% hydrogen and 43.2% oxygen by mass. Its mass spectrum has M⁺ at m/z 74. Its IR spectrum has a strong peak at 1740 cm⁻¹ and no O–H absorption.

items.text: C: 48.6 ÷ 12 = 4.05; H: 8.1 ÷ 1 = 8.1; O: 43.2 ÷ 16 = 2.70. Divide by 2.70 to get 1.5 : 3 : 1, then double to get C₃H₆O₂.
The empirical formula mass is 74, the same as M⁺, so the molecular formula is C₃H₆O₂.
The 1740 cm⁻¹ peak is C=O. There is no O–H absorption, so it is not an acid. With two oxygens it is an ester.
Two singlets in the ratio 3 : 3, at δ 2.0 (CH₃ next to C=O) and δ 3.7 (CH₃ next to O). No splitting means no neighbouring protons.
CH₃COOCH₃, methyl ethanoate. Its ¹³C NMR would have three peaks: CH₃, OCH₃ and C=O.

items: State the evidence for each step.
Show the arithmetic for the formulae.

checks.q: A compound contains 54.5% carbon, 9.1% hydrogen and 36.4% oxygen. Calculate its empirical formula.
A compound has empirical formula CH₂O and its molecular ion peak is at m/z 60. Find its molecular formula.
checks.a: Empirical formula mass = 30. 60 ÷ 30 = 2, so the molecular formula is C₂H₄O₂.

checks.q: An IR spectrum shows a very broad absorption at 2500–3300 cm⁻¹ and a peak at 1710 cm⁻¹. What can you deduce?
checks.a: A carboxylic acid is present: the very broad O–H and the C=O.

blocks.text: You may also use the characteristic reactions of functional groups as evidence, as well as the spectra.

items: Bromine water decolourises: C=C is present.
Fizzing with sodium carbonate: a carboxylic acid is present.
Orange-yellow precipitate with 2,4-DNP: a carbonyl compound.
Silver mirror with Tollens' reagent: an aldehyde.
Orange to green with acidified dichromate on warming: a primary or secondary alcohol, or an aldehyde.

blocks.text: Use these results together with the formula and spectra to confirm the structure.
